text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging network-oncall: potential AZ14 networking degradation affecting IPv6 flows. Alert group: v6_path_mtu_error_rate > 5% over 10m. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1848054321
maria: Ack. I'm on it - taking first touch.
maria: Quick summary from dashboards: AZ14 egress shows spike in ICMPv6 "Packet too big" counters, retransmits up for customer uploads, healthchecks failing intermittently. IPv4 paths look mostly stable.
charlie-support: Getting customer reports: some customers in EU region reporting failed S3-like uploads, timeouts on large file pushes. They say retry works sometimes.
maria: Reproduced a failure from within AZ14: when trying to scp a 25MB file, transfer fails around 14MB and client shows "Message too long" / MTU errors.
lee-neteng: Can you paste the tcpdump/traceroute6 output?
maria: Pasting snippets:

```
root@host:~# traceroute -6 -m 30 storage.redwood.internal
 1  rtr-az14-agg (fe80::1)  0.5 ms
 2  core-az14 (2001:db8:14::1)  1.2 ms
 3  crtr-eu (2001:db8:core::5) 10.8 ms
 4  * * *
```

and tcpdump:
```
17:12:03.123456 IP6 fe80::cafe > 2001:db8:storage: UDP, length 1472
17:12:03.123789 IP6 2001:db8:storage > fe80::cafe: ICMP6, packet too big, mtu 1280
```

maria: Notice ICMPv6 MTU advertised at 1280 while our infra default is 1500 and some hosts are on 9000 (jumbo). That mismatch explains fragmentation issues.
lee-neteng: Hm. Edge egress devices might be rate-limiting ICMPv6 to avoid amplification. If ICMPv6 PTB responses are being dropped or suppressed, PMTUD will fail and large packets will be blackholed.
tina-sre: Are the blackholed flows exclusively over IPv6? Any dualstack clients preferring v6?
charlie-support: Customers show dualstack, many preferring IPv6 when available. Workloads that fell back to IPv4 showed successful uploads.
maria: I'm seeing the same: when we force v4, transfers complete. So root cause hypothesis: an intermediate router (AZ14 egress) is sending ICMPv6 PTB but downstream devices rate-limit or drop further ICMPv6 probes, leading to probe suppression and failed PMTUD for some path combinations and large MTU mismatches (9000 -> 1500 -> 1280).
ops-bot: Incident severity set to P2. Notifying network vendor and escalation list.
maria: Immediate mitigations I propose:
- Apply MTU clamp at AZ14 egress to 1500 for affected prefixes (will avoid PTB dependency)
- Add temporary policy to prefer IPv4 for customer-facing public endpoints from AZ14 (rollback after fix)
- Capture extended tcpdump on aggregator devices for vendor handoff
- Open ticket with provider: include capture + traceroutes + counters

sam: I can implement the MTU clamp. Pushing acl change now, will monitor. ETA 4m.
lee-neteng: Also check router configs for `icmp rate-limit` tuning. If it's too aggressive, vendor may need a patch or config exception for PTB messages.

maria: Update: MTU clamp applied on AZ14-egress-1 and AZ14-egress-2. I see a drop in PTB counters and retransmits are decreasing.
charlie-support: Customer impact reducing, but some sessions still failing if already stalled.
tina-sre: Can we add a short-lived redirect rule: for uploads > 8MB, route to AZ12? That might be disruptive.
sam: Routing change is higher impact. I'd prefer MTU clamp + IPv4-preference rollback for public endpoints.

maria: Rolling IPv4-preference policy to public edge for affected prefmap entries (only for AZ14-originating flows). Will take 2m.

incidents-bot: Automatic note: oncall handoff requested. maria requested handoff to sam at 17:30 UTC.
maria: Handoff to @sam - summary: applied MTU clamp, added IPv4 preference for customer public endpoints from AZ14. Captures uploaded at https://storage.redwood/incident-1848054321/pkt-capture.pcap. Vendor ticket #VN-9832 created.

sam: Taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and coordinate vendor comms. Any ETA from vendor?
lee-neteng: Vendor acknowledged, investigating potential buggy behavior in their jumbo frame offload module when handling ICMPv6 PTB. They want capture + device config.
sam: Good. I'll add our config diff. Also bump tcp_keepalive and short-term retry windows for client-facing LB to reduce customer pain.
charlie-support: Notifying affected customers with status update: brief note explaining transient IPv6 transfer failures, we're routing around via IPv4 and applying fixes. ETA for full resolution currently TBD.

maria: Logged mitigation steps under incident doc. Next steps post-mitigation:
- Coordinate vendor patch/firmware rollout
- Add monitoring for ICMPv6 PTB suppression (alert when PTB counters exceed threshold)
- Review our end-to-end MTU policy: ensure consistent MTU/smallest-MTU advertisement chain or enable reliable PMTUD fallback (dp-8021q shim?)
- Consider adding explicit MTU clamp rules as part of AZ rollout playbook

tina-sre: Customer impact estimate: ~1200 API requests failed across 3 regions for 18 minutes peak. Two enterprise customers had 5-10 user-facing failures each; support is handling refunds/credits via existing SLO process.

sam: Last check: retransmit rates back to baseline, traceroutes show stable hops. I'll keep watch and close when vendor confirms fix or we roll patch.

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach postmortem checklist items to the incident and assign owners.

sam: Thanks all. I'll keep the thread updated. Leaving note to close once vendor delivers patch or we confirm persistent metric stability for 24h.

incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place, monitoring. Severity downgraded to P3 at 18:05 UTC.
